newsitem.title: USA: AMEX takes legal action vs Visa in Chile.
newsitem.headline: AMEX takes legal action vs Visa in Chile.

text.p: American Express Co said on Thursday it had taken legal action against Visa in Chile, alleging anti-competitive practices.

American Express, which has filed legal complaints against its rival credit card issuer in other Latin American countries previously, alleged that Visa has effectively limited card industry competition by restricting the products its member banks can offer to customers.
American Express said it filed a complaint with the Chilean anti-trust authorities.

"Visa is attempting to limit Chilean banks' and consumers' freedom of choice among card products," said Gonzalo Ruiz, American Express vice president and general manager for Latin America and the Caribbean.

Visa was not immediately available for comment, but last month it denied American Express allegations that it had engaged in anti-competitive practices in Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Colombia and Puerto Rico.
Visa said it "has not introduced any statute that prohibits members of Visa from emiting (credit) cards of the competition."
American Express said that in Argentina, the National Commission for the Defense of Competition had opened an investigation into its allegations against Visa.

It said that in Brazil, Aurelio Wander Bastos, secretary of economic law of the Ministry of Justice, had said his office would move to an administrative proceeding against Visa by the Council of Economic Defense.
